settings.content: Brand & Visual Guidelines v1.0, Section Five. These five are fixed by the guide — 60% Half White, 30% Deep Purple, 10% Gold, held on every surface. They are theme settings so a future rebrand has one place to change them, not because day-to-day editing should touch them.

settings.label: Deep Purple
settings.info: All body text. Dark packaging fields.

settings.label: Royal Purple
settings.info: The mark, rules, sub-labels. Never running text — fails contrast below 18px.

settings.label: Pale Lilac
settings.info: Tint blocks, table fills, disabled states.

settings.label: Gold
settings.info: One accent per surface. Foil, rules, buttons. Never more than a tenth of a surface.

settings.label: Light Gold
settings.info: Gold on dark grounds only, where #C2A053 goes muddy.

settings.content: Section Six. Fraunces for the wordmark and headlines (200–300, never bold), Karla for body and labels, IBM Plex Mono for every number a customer might check. Loaded directly from Google Fonts in layout/theme.liquid rather than Shopify's font_picker — Fraunces' variable optical-size axis and IBM Plex Mono are not confirmed entries in Shopify's curated font library, and guessing at picker IDs risked silently falling back to a wrong face. Swap to font_picker later if you confirm both are listed in Shopify's font panel.

Section Two — Construction. The mark's geometry (arc angles, ring radii, seed size) is fixed by the guide and is not exposed here: it is precomputed once in snippets/mark.liquid, verified against the site's Python generator, and never recalculated at render time. Liquid has no trigonometric functions, so recomputing it live is not an option — this keeps the construction correct by making it impossible to edit into an off-spec shape.
